query_title: Chat editors are not affected by `accessibility.dimUnfocused.enabled`
query_body: - Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.44.2 - VS Code Version: 1.116.0 - OS Version: Linux x64 6.18.18-1-MANJARO - Feature: UI/UX, accessibility - Selected model: any, unrelated - Logs: n/a ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Enable `accessibility.dimUnfocused.enabled` 2. Toggle chat 3. Move 2 chats into editor area 4. Arrange editors around, ask AI to generate some sample output or open existing. 5. Focus one chat as editor view ### Issue A lot of colors are the same - instead dimmed - for inactive chats as for normal chats. Code/terminal outputs seems to work properly, but all other text doesn't.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: 🤖 Thanks for the report — this is a real gap. The dim-unfocused feature uses an explicit CSS allowlist (`unfocusedViewDimmingContribution.ts`) and chat editors aren't covered yet. This is tracked by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issue

query_title: Copilot Chat renders `./...` inside inline code as a parent-folder inline reference
query_body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: built-in VS Code `copilot` extension from `C:\Program Files\Microsoft VS Code\fcf604774b\resources\app\extensions\copilot`; `code --list-extensions --show-versions` does not list `GitHub.copilot-chat`
- VS Code Version: 1.125.1 (`fcf604774b9f2674b473065736ee75077e256353`, x64)
- OS Version: Windows 11 Pro 25H2, OS build 26200.8246, Windows Feature Experience Pack 1000.26100.297.0
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Chat panel, Ask mode / normal chat response rendering
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Custom API via UnifyChatProvider, GPT-5.5
- Logs: I have an exported `chat.json`; relevant excerpt is included below.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open VS Code with a workspace nested inside a named parent folder, for example:

```text
C:\Users\<user>\Desktop\repro-parent\repro-workspace
```

2. Open Copilot Chat.

3. Ask Copilot Chat to repeat a command containing `./...` inside inline code:

```text
Please repeat this exact command in inline code: `go test ./...`
```

4. If it does not reproduce on the first try, add workspace/file context and ask again:

```text
The correct command is `go test ./...`. Repeat only the command in inline code.
```

Expected:

The chat response should visibly render exactly:

```text
go test ./...
```

Actual:

The stored model/tool-round response is correct, but the rendered chat message can replace `./..` with an inline file/folder reference to the parent directory and leave the final `.` as text.

In my case the workspace was under:

```text
C:\Users\gyli\Desktop\Misc-local\pylink\jlink-cli
```

The parent folder was `pylink`, so the UI rendered the command as:

```text
go test pylink.
```

Evidence from the exported chat JSON:

The stored final response for request 8 is correct:

```json
"response": "μ¡úτí«σåàσ«╣μÿ»∩╝Ü\n\n`go test ./...`"
```

But the rendered response parts were split into text + inlineReference + text:

```json
[
{ "value": "μ¡úτí«σåàσ«╣μÿ»∩╝Ü\n\n`go test " },
{
"kind": "inlineReference",
"inlineReference": {
"fsPath": "c:\\Users\\gyli\\Desktop\\Misc-local\\pylink",
"path": "/C:/Users/gyli/Desktop/Misc-local/pylink",
"scheme": "file"
}
},
{ "value": ".`" }
]
```

This appears to turn `./...` into:

```text
./.. -> inlineReference to parent folder "pylink"
. -> remaining literal dot
```

Impact:

- The visible chat output changes the literal content of a command inside inline code.
- It makes users think the model generated the wrong command even when the stored response is correct.
- `go test ./...` is a common Go command, so this is easy to hit in development chats.
- The same issue may affect other command tokens containing `./...` or similar relative path syntax.

Possible implementation clue:

This looks related to chat inline reference annotation/linkification rather than model output. It may be near chat inline reference handling in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/widget/annotations.ts` or `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatMarkdownContentPart.ts`. There appears to already be coverage for inline references inside backtick code spans, but `./...` may be a missing edge case where `./..` is recognized as a path reference before/while code-span handling runs.

evidence.evidence_excerpt:
🤖 Thanks for the detailed report and the trace through the exported chat JSON — that made the root cause very clear.

This is the same underlying issue as https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/322469: the file-path linkifier applies it

query_title: Regression: Postman extension fails to load items on VS Code 1.128.0 ("Unable to load items. Retry")
query_body:
## Summary

After updating Visual Studio Code to `1.128.0`, the Postman extension no longer loads its items correctly on Windows.

The extension shows the message:

`Unable to load items. Retry`

Clicking `Retry` has no effect, and the extension remains stuck without loading any content.

Downgrading VS Code back to `1.127.x` restores normal behavior immediately.

---

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install and use the Postman extension in VS Code on Windows
2. Update VS Code to version `1.128.0`
3. Open the Postman extension sidebar/view
4. Wait for the extension to load workspace items
5. Observe the error message
6. Click `Retry`

---

## Actual result

- The extension shows: `Unable to load items. Retry`
- Clicking `Retry` does nothing
- No items are loaded
- The extension remains unusable in this state

---

## Expected result

The Postman extension should load items normally and allow access to workspace content, as it did before the VS Code update.

---

## Regression

Yes, this appears to be a regression.

- Works on: `VS Code 1.127.x`
- Fails on: `VS Code 1.128.0`

The issue disappears completely after downgrading VS Code from `1.128.0` to `1.127.x`.

---

## Environment

- VS Code: `1.128.0 (user setup)`
- Commit: `fc3def6774c76082adf699d366f31a557ce5573f`
- Date: `2026-07-07T15:14:24-07:00`
- Electron: `42.5.0`
- ElectronBuildId: `14525058`
- Chromium: `148.0.7778.271`
- Node.js: `24.17.0`
- V8: `14.8.178.33-electron.0`
- OS: `Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200`

---

## Troubleshooting already attempted

I tried the following before identifying the VS Code version as the likely cause:

- Restarted extensions
- Reinstalled the Postman extension

These steps did not resolve the issue while using VS Code `1.128.0`.

---

## Workaround

Downgraded VS Code to `1.127.x`.

After downgrading, the Postman extension started working normally again without any additional changes.

---

## Impact

This issue prevents the extension from loading workspace items at all, which makes it effectively unusable on VS Code `1.128.0`.

---

## Additional notes

Based on the behavior and the successful downgrade test, this looks like a compatibility issue or regression triggered specifically by VS Code `1.128.0` on Windows.

If helpful, I can also provide:

- Postman extension logs
- VS Code Developer Tools console output
- Screenshots of the error state

A recurring JavaScript error appears in `renderer.log` prior to crashes:

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Update VS Code to 1.129 via apt
2. Launch VS Code (from terminal or desktop — both paths exhibit the same behavior)
3. Use VS Code normally (open files, edit, switch tabs)
4. **Intermittently**, the window crashes with "窗口意外终止(原因: \"crashed\", 代码: \"135\")"
5. Crashpad generates a `.dmp` file in `~/.config/Code/Crashpad/completed/`

## Key Logs

### renderer.log — Recurring JS error (appears 8+ times before crashes)

```
[error] Cannot read properties of null (reading 'left'): TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'left')
at w_t.prepareRender (vscode-file://vscode-app/usr/share/code/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js:519:79187)
at JTt.prepareRender (vscode-file://vscode-app/usr/share/code/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js:519:31984)
at Object.prepareRender (vscode-file://vscode-app/usr/share/code/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js:671:22798)

at h9e.e [as _runner] (vscode-file://vscode-app/usr/share/code/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js:671:26591)
at h9e.execute (vscode-file://vscode-app/usr/share/code/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js:439:3974)

```

This error occurs in the **view rendering pipeline** (`prepareRender`), suggesting a DOM/view model element is unexpectedly `null` when `.left` is accessed.

### main.log — No obvious crash signature

```
2026-07-16 14:10:43.192 [info] StorageMainService: creating application shared storage
2026-07-16 14:10:43.260 [info] update#setState idle
```

## What was ruled out

3. Check if the `MaxListenersExceededWarning` EventEmitter leak is related to the crash

query_title: Flaky git smoke tests: 'opens notebook diff...' timeout and 'rename/delete conflict' assertion
query_body:
Two `git smoke test` cases in `extensions/git/src/test/smoke.test.ts` are flaky and have been temporarily skipped so they stop blocking unrelated PRs (observed on #327131, which changes only chat dictation code and does not touch `extensions/git`).

### Skipped tests
1. **`opens notebook diff and file from active notebook editor`** — times out after 60000ms:
```
Error: Timeout of 60000ms exceeded. For async tests and hooks, ensure "done()" is called; if returning a Promise, ensure it resolves.
at extensions/git/out/test/smoke.test.js
```
2. **`rename/delete conflict`** — assertion failure on the working-tree change count:
```
AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected values to be strictly equal:
1 !== 0
at extensions/git/src/test/smoke.test.ts:203:10
```

query_title: structuredClone() uses wrong context in vm.runInContext()
query_body:
### Version

```text
Darwin Silmaril.home 23.6.0 Darwin Kernel Version 23.6.0: Wed Jul 31 20:49:46 PDT 2024; root:xnu-10063.141.1.700.5~1/RELEASE_ARM64_T8103 arm64
```

### Subsystem

vm

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

```js
const vm = require('node:vm');

const context = vm.createContext({ structuredClone });
const result = vm.runInContext('structuredClone(new Error()) instanceof Error', context);

console.log('match:', result);
```

### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

100%

### What is the expected behavior? Why is that the expected behavior?

`match: true` because `structuredClone` should use the context of the VM for the prototype of the produced `Error` instance.

### What do you see instead?

```match: false```

Additional investigation shows that the produced `Error` uses the prototype of the main runtime. Ie. a context escape, which would be a security error, if not for the disclaimer not to run untrusted code.

### Additional information

This issue also applies to all other cloneable types like `Map`. Even `Object` fails `instanceof`:

```js
structuredClone({}) instanceof Object // <= equals false inside VM
```

FYI, this causes problems when running tests in jest, which use the VM to run tests.

### What is the problem this feature will solve?

query_title: Path metavars inside macro expansions can't be used to refer to macros in some context
query_body:
<!--
Thank you for filing a bug report! 🐛 Please provide a short summary of the bug,
along with any information you feel relevant to replicating the bug.
-->

I tried this code:

```rust
macro_rules! a {
($a:path) => {
const _: () = $a!();
};
}

a! {std::println}
```

I expected to see this happen: An error that `println!()` is not allowed in const contexts.

Instead, this happened: ``expected one of `.`, `;`, `?`, `where`, or an operator, found `!` ``

However the following does correctly parse:

```rust
macro_rules! a {
($a:path) => {
const _: () = {
$a!();
};
};
}

a! {std::println}
```

query_title: [Low] unsafe_block: Unnecessary unsafe block in unwind/src/unwinding.rs (line 74)
query_body:
[[ I tried this code: ```rust // 代码来源:rust/library/unwind/src/unwinding.rs (line 74) // 缺陷:使用不必要的unsafe块进行指针转换,可通过安全方式实现 let ctx = unsafe { &mut *(ctx as *mut UnwindContext<'_>) }; ``` I expected to see this happen: * * 移除不必要的unsafe代码块,通过Rust的安全类型转换或API实现相同逻辑(例如:若`ctx`的类型本身支持安全的可变引用转换,直接使用类型系统约束的安全操作); * 避免无必要的unsafe使用,降低代码的安全风险与攻击面。* Instead, this happened: * * 缺陷类型:不必要的unsafe代码块(Low风险,对应比赛评价权重1); * 实际行为:使用unsafe块进行可通过安全方式完成的指针转换,增加了代码的安全风险与攻击面; * 影响:不必要的unsafe会降低代码的可维护性,且可能掩盖潜在的类型安全问题,违背Rust“最小化unsafe范围”的编码规范。* ### Meta `rustc --version --verbose`: ``` rustc 1.94.0-nightly (e7d44143a 2025-12-24)binary: rustccommit-hash: e7d44143a12a526488e4f0c0d7ea8e62a4fe9354commit-date: 2025-12-24host: x86_64-pc-windows-msvcrelease: 1.94.0-nightlyLLVM version: 21.1.8 ```
Backtrace

```

Note (No runtime backtrace for this issue)

This issue is a code规范 defect (unnecessary unsafe block) rather than a runtime error, so no backtrace is generated. The risk lies in avoidable unsafe usage that increases code complexity and potential vulnerabilities.

```

query_title: Deriving Default for non-default generics should work in trivial cases
query_body:
<!--
Thank you for filing a bug report! 🐛 Please provide a short summary of the bug,
along with any information you feel relevant to replicating the bug.
-->

```rust
struct NoDefault {}

#[derive(Default)]
struct VecHolder<T> {
data: Vec<T>,
}

fn main() {
let x: VecHolder<NoDefault> = VecHolder::default();
}
```

This produces an error:
```
error[E0277]: the trait bound `NoDefault: Default` is not satisfied
--> <source>:9:35
|
9 | let x: VecHolder<NoDefault> = VecHolder::default();
| ^^^^^^^^^ the trait `Default` is not implemented for `NoDefault`
|
help: the trait `Default` is implemented for `VecHolder<T>`
--> <source>:3:10
|
3 | #[derive(Default)]
| ^^^^^^^
note: required for `VecHolder<NoDefault>` to implement `Default`
--> <source>:3:10
|
3 | #[derive(Default)]
| ^^^^^^^ unsatisfied trait bound introduced in this `derive` macro
help: consider annotating `NoDefault` with `#[derive(Default)]`
|
1 + #[derive(Default)]
2 | struct NoDefault {}
|
```

I expected this to compile, because `Default` implementation for `Vec<T>` does not require `T: Default`
Moreover, you can define it trivially yourself:
```rust
struct NoDefault {}

struct VecHolder<T> {
data: Vec<T>,
}

impl<T> Default for VecHolder<T> {
fn default() -> Self {
Self {
data: Default::default()
}
}
}

fn main() {
let x: VecHolder<NoDefault> = VecHolder::default();
}
```
...and this works.

`rustc --version --verbose`:
I'm using Godbolt compiler 1.93.0 (https://godbolt.org/z/GMd1nvMjz), but it's the same with pretty much any other major version, including current nightly

query_title: ICE: generic_const_parameter_types const referencing lifetime
query_body:
### Code ```Rust #![feature(adt_const_params, unsized_const_params, generic_const_parameter_types)] #![allow(incomplete_features)] trait Object<'a, const N: &'a u32> {} fn binder(param: &dyn for<'a> Object<'a, true>) {} fn main() {} ``` Discovered in https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/152931 Three stages of what "should" happen: - Currently it should probably `//@ check-pass`, ignoring the type error, instead of ICEing. - Next, `feature(generic_const_parameter_types)` should probably disallow ConstArgHasType obligations to reference lifetimes introduced by a sibling in the binder that introduces the const parameter (i.e. ban `for<'a, const N: &'a u32>`). - Eventually, in a possible cool future world, generic_const_parameter_types will allow that, and it should type error on the fact that `true` is not a `&'a u32`. ### Meta tested on my rustc checkout https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/commit/d8b2222b11fc03a31d43707c8c9006f025809ece and also ices on stable: `rustc --version --verbose`: ``` rustc 1.93.1 (01f6ddf75 2026-02-11) binary: rustc commit-hash: 01f6ddf7588f42ae2d7eb0a2f21d44e8e96674cf commit-date: 2026-02-11 host: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu release: 1.93.1 LLVM version: 21.1.8 ``` ### Error output

query_title: [ICE]: `DispatchFromDyn` with a `repr(align)` type causes "receiver type has unsupported layout"
